choices: Read receipts were presumably designed to reassure senders that their message had been read.
A sixteen-year-old with a weekend job at a café, for instance, may belong to a staff group in which shifts are swapped late at night.
Without them, the argument goes, people could ignore inconvenient messages indefinitely while pretending not to have noticed them.
Families, friends and teams each develop unwritten rules about how quickly one should answer, and newcomers usually learn them only by breaking them.
